\# CLINICAL EVALUATION PLAN (CEP)  
\#\# Patient-Facing Digital Functional & Respiratory Assessment Tools

\*\*Devices under evaluation\*\*    
\- Breathscope    
\- V27 Biomechanics Engine (GaitScope)    
\- ROM Lens    
\- ROM Lens CS (Cervical)

\*\*Manufacturer / Legal Manufacturer\*\*    
Virtual Care Solution (virtualcaresolution.de)    
Independent Research & Development  

\*\*Document Version\*\*    
1.0 – September 2026  

\*\*Prepared in accordance with\*\*    
\- Regulation (EU) 2017/745 (MDR) – Article 61 & Annex XIV Part A    
\- MDCG 2020-1 – Guidance on Clinical Evaluation of Medical Device Software    
\- MDCG 2020-5, 2020-6, 2020-13  

\*\*Clinical Lead / Sponsoring Site\*\*    
AMEOS Klinikum Inntal & AMEOS Reha Klinikum Inntal    
Dr. med. univ. Margarete Liebmann, Ärztliche Direktorin  

\---

\#\# 1\. Document Control & Purpose

This Clinical Evaluation Plan defines the strategy, methods, data sources, acceptance criteria and documentation approach for the clinical evaluation of the four patient-facing tools listed above.

The CEP ensures that clinical evidence is generated and appraised in a systematic, transparent and MDR-compliant manner to demonstrate:  
\- Conformity with relevant General Safety and Performance Requirements (GSPRs)  
\- Positive benefit-risk ratio  
\- Achievement of the claimed clinical benefits when used as intended

This plan will be updated throughout the device lifecycle and forms the basis for the Clinical Evaluation Report (CER) and the Post-Market Clinical Follow-up (PMCF) Plan.

\---

\#\# 2\. Device Description & Intended Purpose

\#\#\# 2.1 Device Overview

| Tool | Core Technology | Primary Output | Use Environment |  
|------|-----------------|---------------|-----------------|  
| \*\*Breathscope\*\* | Microphone-based acoustic analysis | Respiratory pattern metrics, trend indicators | Clinic \+ Home |  
| \*\*V27 Biomechanics Engine\*\* | Camera-based motion analysis | Knee/hip angles, cadence, stride length, asymmetry, risk score, step count | Clinic \+ Home |  
| \*\*ROM Lens\*\* | Rear-camera / environment motion tracking | Joint range-of-motion (°) | Clinic \+ Home |  
| \*\*ROM Lens CS\*\* | Front-camera (selfie) cervical motion tracking | Cervical flexion, extension, rotation, lateral flexion (°) | Clinic \+ Home |

All tools are designed as \*\*cloud-free / local-only processing\*\* applications. Data remain on the user’s device unless explicitly exported by the user.

\#\#\# 2.2 Intended Purpose (Current Working Statements)

\*\*Common intended purpose framework\*\*    
Patient-facing digital tools intended to support the measurement, monitoring and trend observation of selected functional movement parameters and respiratory patterns in adult patients. The tools are intended to assist healthcare professionals and patients in the assessment of functional status and respiratory trends as part of a broader clinical evaluation. They are \*\*not\*\* intended to provide a medical diagnosis, to autonomously recommend treatment, or to replace clinical judgement.

\*\*Specific claims (to be refined and locked before CER)\*\*    
\- Screening and trend monitoring of respiratory patterns (Breathscope)    
\- Objective measurement and monitoring of selected gait and lower-limb kinematic parameters (V27)    
\- Measurement of joint range of motion (ROM Lens)    
\- Measurement of cervical range of motion (ROM Lens CS)

\*\*Target population\*\*    
Adult patients (≥ 18 years) in psychosomatic, psychosomatic rehabilitation, orthopaedic, neurological or related care settings who are able to perform the required movements or breathing manoeuvres safely and provide informed consent.

\*\*Contraindications / Limitations\*\*    
Acute medical instability, severe cognitive impairment preventing safe use or informed consent, conditions that make reference measurements unsafe.

\*\*Important regulatory note\*\*    
The intended purpose deliberately avoids diagnostic or therapeutic decision-making claims in order to keep the risk profile proportionate and the clinical evidence requirements focused on measurement performance and clinical utility.

\---

\#\# 3\. Identification of Relevant GSPRs Requiring Clinical Data

The following General Safety and Performance Requirements (Annex I MDR) are expected to require support from clinical data:

| GSPR | Description | Clinical Data Needed |  
|------|-------------|----------------------|  
| 1 | Devices shall achieve the performance intended by the manufacturer | Performance claims (accuracy, reliability of measurements) |  
| 8 | Risks related to the design and characteristics of materials / software | Usability, use-error analysis, residual risks |  
| 14 | Construction and design – measurement function | Accuracy, precision, measurement error |  
| 17 | Electronic programmable systems / software | Clinical performance of software outputs |  
| 22 | Devices for measuring functions | Metrological performance, reliability |  
| 23 | Information supplied by the manufacturer | Clarity of instructions, residual risk communication |

A full GSPR matrix will be maintained and updated in the technical documentation.

\---

\#\# 4\. Clinical Benefits & Outcome Parameters

\*\*Claimed clinical benefits\*\*    
\- Provision of objective, reproducible functional and respiratory measurements that can support clinical assessment and patient self-monitoring    
\- Enabling trend observation over time (admission → mid-stay → discharge → home)    
\- Supporting shared decision-making and continuity of care through patient-generated data    
\- Offering a privacy-preserving (cloud-free) alternative to conventional measurement tools

\*\*Primary clinical outcome parameters\*\*    
\- Measurement accuracy / agreement with reference methods (bias, limits of agreement)    
\- Reliability (ICC, SEM, Minimal Detectable Change)    
\- Usability (System Usability Scale)    
\- Feasibility (completion rates, time burden, patient acceptance)    
\- Correlation with clinical status indicators (pain, mobility, fatigue, functional scores) where available

\---

\#\# 5\. Clinical Development Strategy & Evidence Pyramid

\`\`\`  
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  
│                    CLINICAL EVIDENCE PYRAMID                │  
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤  
│  Level 1 (Highest)                                          │  
│  Device-specific clinical investigation / validation study │  
│  → AMEOS Inntal PhD Pilot (criterion validity \+ reliability)│  
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤  
│  Level 2                                                    │  
│  High-quality literature on comparable measurement methods  │  
│  \+ Usability & real-world feasibility data                  │  
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤  
│  Level 3                                                    │  
│  Technical verification & validation, bench testing         │  
│  State-of-the-art analysis                                  │  
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  
\`\`\`

\*\*Primary evidence source\*\*    
The ongoing / planned prospective validation and reliability study at AMEOS Klinikum Inntal / AMEOS Reha Klinikum Inntal under the clinical leadership of Dr. med. univ. Margarete Liebmann constitutes the core clinical investigation data for these tools.

\*\*Supporting sources\*\*    
\- Systematic literature review on camera-based ROM / gait analysis and microphone-based respiratory monitoring    
\- Technical verification & validation reports    
\- Usability engineering file (IEC 62366-1)    
\- Risk management file (ISO 14971\)

\*\*Equivalence\*\*    
Equivalence to existing marketed devices will be explored but is not expected to be the primary route, given the novel cloud-free architecture and specific algorithms. Any equivalence claim will follow MDCG 2020-5 strictly (technical \+ clinical characteristics).

\---

\#\# 6\. Clinical Evaluation Methodology

\#\#\# 6.1 Stages of Clinical Evaluation (per MDCG 2020-1)

\`\`\`  
1\. Planning          → This CEP  
2\. Data Identification → Literature \+ clinical investigation \+ technical data  
3\. Data Appraisal    → Methodological quality, relevance, contribution  
4\. Data Analysis     → Synthesis against GSPRs and benefit-risk  
5\. Documentation     → CER \+ continuous update via PMCF  
\`\`\`

\#\#\# 6.2 Three Pillars of Clinical Evidence for MDSW (MDCG 2020-1)

| Pillar | Definition | Planned Evidence for these Tools |  
|--------|------------|----------------------------------|  
| \*\*1. Scientific Validity\*\* | Association between software output and clinical condition / physiological parameter | Literature \+ clinical correlation analyses in the pilot study |  
| \*\*2. Technical / Analytical Performance\*\* | Accuracy, reliability, precision of output generation | Criterion validity vs reference standards \+ reliability metrics (ICC, SEM, MDC, Bland-Altman) |  
| \*\*3. Clinical Performance\*\* | Achievement of intended clinical benefit in the target population | Usability, feasibility, clinical utility, patient/clinician acceptance in real care setting |

\#\#\# 6.3 Acceptance Criteria (Preliminary)

\- ICC ≥ 0.75 (good reliability) for primary measurement parameters    
\- Acceptable limits of agreement in Bland-Altman analysis relative to clinical relevance    
\- System Usability Scale (SUS) mean score ≥ 68 (above average)    
\- High completion rates and acceptable time burden    
\- No serious adverse events attributable to tool use    
\- Positive benefit-risk determination by the clinical evaluation team

Final acceptance criteria will be locked in the statistical analysis plan of the clinical investigation.

\---

\#\# 7\. Clinical Investigation Outline (Core Evidence Source)

\*\*Study title\*\*    
Validity, Reliability and Clinical Utility of Patient-Facing Cloud-Free Digital Tools for Respiratory and Functional Movement Assessment in a Psychosomatic and Psychosomatic Rehabilitation Population

\*\*Design\*\*    
Prospective, single-centre (with possible multi-site extension), observational validation and feasibility study with embedded reliability assessments.

\*\*Setting\*\*    
AMEOS Klinikum Inntal (acute psychosomatic) and AMEOS Reha Klinikum Inntal.

\*\*Key elements\*\*    
\- Criterion validity against established reference methods    
\- Test-retest and inter-rater reliability    
\- Usability (SUS) and qualitative feedback    
\- Longitudinal measurements (admission – mid-stay – pre-discharge ± home)    
\- Mapping of results to the three MDCG 2020-1 pillars and relevant GSPRs

\*\*Sample size\*\*    
Preliminary target 60–120 patients depending on primary endpoint (to be confirmed after pilot reliability data and statistical consultation).

\*\*Ethics & Governance\*\*    
Ethics committee approval, informed consent, data protection impact assessment, clinical leadership by Dr. Liebmann.

\---

\#\# 8\. Literature Search Strategy

A systematic literature search will be performed and documented according to a pre-specified protocol:

\- Databases: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane, IEEE Xplore, Google Scholar    
\- Key concepts: camera-based range of motion, smartphone gait analysis, microphone respiratory monitoring, validity, reliability, psychosomatic / rehabilitation populations    
\- Inclusion/exclusion criteria, date limits, language limits and quality appraisal methods will be defined in a separate literature search protocol.    
\- Both favourable and unfavourable data will be included.

\---

\#\# 9\. Benefit-Risk Analysis Approach

The clinical evaluation will:  
1\. Identify all known and foreseeable risks (from risk management file \+ clinical data)  
2\. Quantify residual risks after risk control measures  
3\. Weigh residual risks against the claimed clinical benefits  
4\. Conclude whether the benefit-risk ratio is acceptable when the devices are used as intended

The conclusion will be documented in the CER and updated via PMCF.

\---

\#\# 10\. Post-Market Clinical Follow-up (PMCF) Linkage

This CEP already anticipates PMCF needs. A separate PMCF Plan will be created after the initial CER and will address:  
\- Continued performance in routine use at AMEOS Inntal and additional sites  
\- Home-use data collection  
\- Detection of emerging risks or off-label use  
\- Confirmation of long-term benefit-risk acceptability

PMCF findings will feed back into updates of the CER.

\---

\#\# 11\. Roles & Responsibilities

| Role | Responsibility |  
|------|----------------|  
| Clinical Principal Investigator | Dr. med. univ. Margarete Liebmann – overall clinical oversight |  
| Clinical Evaluation Team | Multidisciplinary team including clinical, methodological and regulatory expertise |  
| Manufacturer | Virtual Care Solution – technical documentation ownership, risk management, CER maintenance |  
| PhD Candidate / Study Coordinator | Day-to-day execution of the clinical investigation, data analysis, manuscript preparation |

\---

\#\# 12\. Timeline & Update Cycle

| Milestone | Target |  
|-----------|--------|  
| CEP finalisation & approval | Q4 2026 |  
| Ethics approval & study start | Q1–Q2 2027 |  
| Primary data collection complete | Q4 2027 / Q1 2028 |  
| First full CER | Within 3 months of primary analysis |  
| PMCF Plan | Concurrent with first CER |  
| CER updates | At least annually or when significant new data emerge |

\---

\#\# 13\. Conclusion of this CEP

This Clinical Evaluation Plan establishes a clear, MDR-compliant pathway to generate high-quality clinical evidence for Breathscope, V27 Biomechanics Engine, ROM Lens and ROM Lens CS.  

The planned clinical investigation at AMEOS Klinikum Inntal under the leadership of Dr. Liebmann is designed to deliver the core device-specific data required for scientific validity, technical performance and clinical performance, thereby supporting a robust Clinical Evaluation Report and future conformity assessment.

The plan will be reviewed and updated as new information becomes available.

\---

\*\*Document prepared for regulatory and clinical use\*\*    
Virtual Care Solution – September 2026  

\*This CEP is a living document and forms part of the technical documentation under MDR Annex II.\*

\# PhD / Doktorarbeit & Pilot Study Proposal    
\#\# Patient-Facing Digital Functional & Respiratory Assessment Tools    
\#\#\# Breathscope · V27 Biomechanics Engine · ROM Lens · ROM Lens CS (Cervical)

\*\*Sponsoring Site / Clinical Lead\*\*    
AMEOS Klinikum Inntal (Psychosomatik) & AMEOS Reha Klinikum Inntal    
Simbach am Inn, Bayern  

\*\*Ärztliche Direktorin / Clinical Champion\*\*    
Dr. med. univ. Margarete Liebmann    
Ärztliche Direktorin der AMEOS Klinika in Simbach am Inn  

\*\*Prepared for\*\*    
Dr. med. univ. Margarete Liebmann and the AMEOS Inntal clinical & research leadership  

\*\*Date\*\*    
September 2026  

\*\*Tools under investigation (patient-facing only)\*\*    
\- Breathscope – microphone-based respiratory screening & trend monitoring    
\- V27 Biomechanics Engine (GaitScope) – real-time gait and movement metrics    
\- ROM Lens – camera-based range-of-motion tracker (rear / environment mode)    
\- ROM Lens CS – Cervical ROM assessment (selfie / front-camera mode)  

All other Virtual Care Solution tools (EncounterGuard, MyMEDFIT/VERITAS, RegIntel, Maturity Compass, etc.) remain clinician- or administrator-facing and are \*\*not\*\* part of this patient-facing pilot / PhD project.

\---

\#\# 1\. Background and Rationale

Patients in psychosomatic and psychosomatic rehabilitation settings frequently present with:  
\- Functional movement restrictions and altered gait patterns  
\- Cervical and upper-body tension / restricted range of motion  
\- Respiratory dysregulation linked to anxiety, depression, chronic pain, and somatisation

Objective, reproducible, low-burden measurement of these domains is currently limited in routine care. Existing solutions are often:  
\- Cloud-dependent (raising data-protection and sovereignty concerns)  
\- Clinician-operated only  
\- Lacking rigorous validity and reliability data under real-world conditions

The proposed patient-facing tools are designed to run fully locally on the patient’s or clinic’s device (cloud-free, privacy-by-design). This creates a unique opportunity to generate high-quality evidence while fully respecting GDPR and digital sovereignty requirements — a priority after recent cyber incidents in the German hospital sector.

\*\*Strategic fit with AMEOS Klinikum Inntal\*\*    
Under the leadership of Dr. Liebmann, the Inntal sites combine acute psychosomatic care, family psychosomatics, transcultural psychosomatics, and psychosomatic rehabilitation. This continuum is ideal for:  
\- Validation across acute → rehab → home-care transition  
\- Patient self-monitoring during and after the stay  
\- Generation of functional and respiratory outcome data that can support quality management and future value-based approaches

\---

\#\# 2\. Primary Research Aim

To evaluate the \*\*validity, reliability, usability, and clinical utility\*\* of four patient-facing, cloud-free digital tools (Breathscope, V27 Biomechanics Engine, ROM Lens, ROM Lens CS) in a psychosomatic and psychosomatic rehabilitation population, generating evidence of the highest methodological quality to support future MDR conformity assessment and routine clinical adoption.

\---

\#\# 3\. Specific Objectives

1\. \*\*Criterion validity\*\*    
   Compare tool-derived metrics against established reference standards (spirometry / respiratory reference methods for Breathscope; optical motion capture or clinical goniometry / validated gait analysis for the biomechanics and ROM tools).

2\. \*\*Reliability\*\*    
   Assess test-retest reliability, inter-rater reliability (where applicable), and measurement error (SEM, MDC, ICC, Bland-Altman).

3\. \*\*Usability & acceptance\*\*    
   Evaluate patient and clinician System Usability Scale (SUS), Technology Acceptance Model constructs, and qualitative feedback.

4\. \*\*Clinical utility & feasibility\*\*    
   Examine completion rates, time burden, correlation with clinical outcomes (pain, mobility, fatigue, functional status, length of stay, discharge destination), and suitability for home-based follow-up.

5\. \*\*Safety & data integrity\*\*    
   Document any adverse events related to tool use and verify local-only data handling.

6\. \*\*MDR-relevant evidence generation\*\*    
   Produce a structured clinical evaluation report aligned with MDR Annex XIV and MDCG guidance on clinical evaluation of software.

\---

\#\# 4\. Study Design

\*\*Design\*\*    
Prospective, single-centre (with possible multi-site extension within AMEOS), observational validation and feasibility study with embedded reliability assessments.    
PhD project structured as a multi-paper thesis.

\*\*Setting\*\*    
AMEOS Klinikum Inntal (acute psychosomatic) and AMEOS Reha Klinikum Inntal (psychosomatic rehabilitation), Simbach am Inn.

\*\*Population\*\*    
Adult patients (≥18 years) admitted for psychosomatic or psychosomatic rehabilitation treatment who are able to provide informed consent and perform the required movements / breathing manoeuvres safely.

\*\*Sample size (preliminary)\*\*    
\- Validity & reliability core analyses: n \= 60–80 (powered for ICC ≥ 0.75 and acceptable limits of agreement)    
\- Usability & feasibility: n \= 100–120    
\- Subgroup analyses (e.g., high pain, respiratory symptoms, cervical focus): planned a priori  

Final sample size will be confirmed after pilot reliability data and statistical consultation.

\*\*Key exclusion criteria\*\*    
Acute medical instability, severe cognitive impairment preventing informed consent or safe tool use, contraindications to the reference measurements.

\---

\#\# 5\. Methods – Highest Validity & Reliability Standards

\#\#\# 5.1 Reference Standards  
\- \*\*Breathscope\*\*: Laboratory or clinic-based spirometry / respiratory inductive plethysmography or equivalent validated respiratory reference (protocol to be finalised with respiratory physiology expertise).  
\- \*\*V27 Biomechanics Engine\*\*: Optical motion capture system or validated clinical gait analysis protocol (3D kinematics where available; otherwise high-quality 2D \+ clinical scales).  
\- \*\*ROM Lens & ROM Lens CS\*\*: Universal goniometer / inclinometer measurements performed by trained assessors following standardised protocols (e.g., cervical ROM according to established clinical standards); dual-assessor design for inter-rater reliability.

\#\#\# 5.2 Measurement Protocol  
\- Standardised instructions and calibration procedures for every tool.  
\- Multiple measurement occasions (e.g., admission, mid-stay, pre-discharge, optional home follow-up).  
\- Blinded or independent reference assessors where feasible.  
\- Randomised or counter-balanced order of digital tool vs. reference measurement to minimise order effects.  
\- Detailed logging of device type, lighting, camera distance, and environmental conditions.

\#\#\# 5.3 Statistical Analysis Plan (high-level)  
\- Intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC 2,1 or 3,1) with 95% confidence intervals.  
\- Bland-Altman plots with limits of agreement and assessment of proportional bias.  
\- Standard error of measurement (SEM) and minimal detectable change (MDC).  
\- Pearson / Spearman correlations with clinical outcomes.  
\- Linear mixed models for longitudinal data.  
\- Pre-specified sensitivity analyses.

\#\#\# 5.4 Qualitative Component  
Semi-structured interviews or focus groups with patients and treating clinicians (physiotherapists, physicians, nurses) on perceived usefulness, barriers, and integration into the therapeutic process.

\#\#\# 5.5 MDR Alignment  
\- Clinical evaluation plan and report structured according to MDR requirements and MDCG 2020-1 / 2020-13 guidance.  
\- Clear intended purpose statements for each tool (screening / trend monitoring / functional assessment support — \*\*not\*\* diagnosis or autonomous treatment decisions).  
\- Risk management file linkage (ISO 14971).  
\- Post-market clinical follow-up (PMCF) considerations already built into the longitudinal design.

\---

\#\# 6\. PhD Structure (Proposed Multi-Paper Thesis)

\*\*Paper 1\*\*    
Technical validation and reliability of ROM Lens and ROM Lens CS (cervical) in a psychosomatic population.

\*\*Paper 2\*\*    
Criterion validity and measurement properties of the V27 Biomechanics Engine against reference gait/movement analysis.

\*\*Paper 3\*\*    
Validity, reliability and feasibility of Breathscope for respiratory trend monitoring in psychosomatic and rehab patients.

\*\*Paper 4\*\*    
Integrated clinical utility, patient acceptance, and implementation findings across the four tools — implications for routine care and digital sovereignty.

\*\*Optional Paper 5\*\*    
Home-based follow-up feasibility and correlation with clinical course after discharge.

Supervision model (suggested):    
\- Clinical supervisor: Dr. med. univ. Margarete Liebmann (AMEOS Inntal)    
\- Methodological / academic supervisor: University partner (to be confirmed — possibilities include Medical University of Graz given existing AMEOS links, or a Bavarian / German university with digital health / rehabilitation expertise)    
\- Technical / digital health co-supervisor if required

\---

\#\# 7\. Clear Implementation Plan

| Phase | Timeline (indicative) | Key Activities |  
|-------|-----------------------|----------------|  
| \*\*0 – Preparation\*\* | Month 0–2 | Ethics submission, study protocol finalisation, staff training, device setup, reference equipment access, statistical analysis plan, patient information materials |  
| \*\*1 – Pilot reliability\*\* | Month 3–4 | Small cohort (n≈15–20) for protocol refinement and initial ICC estimates |  
| \*\*2 – Main validity & reliability\*\* | Month 5–10 | Full recruitment and reference comparisons |  
| \*\*3 – Usability & longitudinal\*\* | Month 6–12 | Concurrent collection of SUS, clinical outcomes, optional home measurements |  
| \*\*4 – Analysis & writing\*\* | Month 11–18 | Statistical analysis, manuscript preparation, clinical evaluation report for MDR |  
| \*\*5 – Dissemination & scale\*\* | Month 16–24 | Publications, internal AMEOS presentation, recommendations for wider rollout |

\*\*Governance\*\*    
\- Study leadership: Dr. Liebmann (Clinical Principal Investigator)    
\- Day-to-day coordination: designated study physician / PhD candidate    
\- Data protection: fully local processing \+ secure institutional handling of any exported research datasets    
\- Regular steering meetings with AMEOS Inntal leadership

\*\*Resources required (high-level)\*\*    
\- PhD candidate (or physician-scientist time)    
\- Access to reference measurement equipment / expertise    
\- Ethics and institutional approval    
\- Minimal IT support (tools are local-first)    
\- Possible small grant for reference measurements or patient incentives

\---

\#\# 8\. Expected Outcomes & Impact

\*\*Scientific\*\*    
\- High-quality validity and reliability data meeting international standards    
\- Peer-reviewed publications    
\- Structured clinical evaluation documentation supporting future MDR conformity assessment

\*\*Clinical (AMEOS Inntal)\*\*    
\- Objective functional and respiratory data integrated into psychosomatic treatment pathways    
\- Patient empowerment through self-monitoring    
\- Evidence base for quality indicators and therapy evaluation    
\- Demonstration of sovereign, privacy-first digital tools in a real clinical environment

\*\*Strategic\*\*    
\- Strengthens AMEOS Inntal’s profile as an innovative, research-active psychosomatic centre    
\- Creates a replicable model for other AMEOS sites    
\- Positions the tools for broader DACH adoption under a strong clinical evidence umbrella

\---

\#\# 9\. Ethical & Regulatory Notes

\- The tools are currently positioned as research prototypes / screening and trend-monitoring aids.    
\- They do \*\*not\*\* provide medical diagnoses or autonomous treatment recommendations.    
\- Full informed consent, ethics committee approval, and data protection impact assessment will be obtained before any patient recruitment.    
\- MDR pathway will be planned in parallel with the clinical evaluation so that evidence generation directly supports regulatory readiness.

\---

\#\# 10\. Next Immediate Steps (requested by Dr. Liebmann)

1\. Formal discussion and endorsement of this synopsis by Dr. Liebmann and AMEOS Inntal leadership.    
2\. Identification of academic co-supervisor / university partner.    
3\. Refinement of reference standard protocols with local expertise (respiratory, physiotherapy, movement analysis).    
4\. Preparation of ethics dossier.    
5\. Confirmation of PhD candidate or physician time allocation.

\---

\*\*Document prepared for Dr. med. univ. Margarete Liebmann\*\*    
AMEOS Klinikum Inntal / AMEOS Reha Klinikum Inntal    
in support of a high-validity, MDR-aligned PhD pilot study on patient-facing digital functional and respiratory assessment tools.

\*Virtual Care Solution – Independent Research & Development\*    
September 2026

# **PhD Strategy and Lung Research Map (Bavaria Region)**

## **Candidate Profile**

Moustafa Ali – Physiotherapist working in rehabilitation with a focus on respiratory therapy and digital health innovation.

Developer of BreathScope, a browser-based respiratory volumetry tool currently used clinically at

Rosenhof Fachklinik.

The project combines:

* Physiotherapy

* Pulmonary rehabilitation

* Digital respiratory measurement

* Browser-based medical technology

This profile places the project at the intersection of clinical rehabilitation and digital health research.

---

# **Proposed PhD Topic**

Digital Volumetric Respiratory Monitoring in Pulmonary Rehabilitation: Development, Validation and Clinical Integration

The research investigates whether digital respiratory volumetry can be used as a continuous physiotherapy assessment tool in rehabilitation settings.

---

# **Research Problem**

Respiratory physiotherapy lacks simple, continuous, objective measurement tools.

Most clinics rely on:

* subjective observation

* respiratory rate counting

* occasional pulmonary tests

Standard pulmonary function tests such as

* Spirometry

* Plethysmography

provide valuable data but are not practical for frequent use during physiotherapy sessions.

As a result, therapy outcomes are often poorly quantified.

---

# **Innovation**

BreathScope is a browser-based respiratory analysis system designed for physiotherapy and pulmonary rehabilitation.

Key characteristics:

* No software installation

* Works in any browser

* Privacy-friendly (local processing possible)

* Easy integration in clinical workflows

Core capabilities:

* respiratory rate monitoring

* breathing amplitude estimation

* breathing pattern analysis

* therapy response tracking

Clinical testing is already occurring at:

Rosenhof Fachklinik

This provides a real-world translational research starting point.

---

# **Initial Study Design**

### **Participants**

60 rehabilitation patients.

### **Target Conditions**

* Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease

* Heart Failure

These are among the most common internal medicine conditions in rehabilitation clinics.

---

### **Measurements**

1. BreathScope respiratory signal analysis

2. Spirometry measurements

3. Functional capacity tests (e.g. 6-Minute Walk Test)

---

### **Research Questions**

1. Can BreathScope estimate breathing amplitude trends related to tidal volume?

2. Can the system detect improvements in respiratory efficiency during physiotherapy?

3. Can respiratory pattern changes predict clinical improvement or deterioration?

---

### **Expected Outcome**

Validation of a digital respiratory monitoring tool for physiotherapy and rehabilitation medicine.

---

# **3-Phase Strategy to Land a Funded PhD (6–12 Months)**

## **Phase 1 – Preparation (Month 1\)**

Prepare the key materials required to approach research groups.

### **Academic CV**

Highlight:

* Physiotherapy education

* Rehabilitation clinical experience

* Respiratory therapy specialization

* Digital health development

* BreathScope project

---

### **Research Proposal (2–3 pages)**

Include:

1. Clinical problem

2. Digital innovation (BreathScope)

3. Study design

4. Clinical impact

---

### **Prototype Demonstration**

Provide:

BreathScope platform link.

Include documentation showing clinical testing in Rosenhof Fachklinik.

This is a major advantage, because most PhD applicants do not have a working prototype.

---

# **Phase 2 – Direct Professor Outreach (Months 2–3)**

Instead of applying only through job portals, contact professors directly.

Target fields:

* pulmonology

* rehabilitation medicine

* digital health

* biomedical engineering

* respiratory physiology

Send:

* short introduction email

* CV

* 2-page proposal

* BreathScope link

Direct contact dramatically increases the probability of receiving PhD supervision offers.

---

# **Phase 3 – Funding and Formal Application (Months 3–12)**

Most PhDs in Germany are paid research positions.

Typical contract:

TV-L E13

Salary range:

€2600–€3200 net per month depending on contract percentage.

Possible funding paths:

### **University Research Positions**

Research assistant PhD contracts.

### **External Grants**

* German Research Foundation

* DAAD

### **EU Research Programs**

Horizon Europe digital health initiatives.

---

# **Regional Lung Research Map (Near Simbach am Inn)**

The strongest regional lung research ecosystem is in Munich.

It centers around the Comprehensive Pneumology Center Munich.

---

## **Munich Lung Research Hub**

The Comprehensive Pneumology Center Munich (CPC-M) is a collaboration between:

* Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich

* Helmholtz Munich

* Asklepios Lung Clinic Gauting

This is one of Europe’s largest lung research networks.

The center focuses on:

* COPD

* lung regeneration

* pulmonary inflammation

* respiratory diagnostics

* digital health approaches

This ecosystem is highly compatible with BreathScope-style digital respiratory monitoring.

---

# **Potential PhD Supervisors**

## **Ali Önder Yildirim**

Institute for Lung Health and Immunity

Helmholtz Munich / LMU Munich

Research focus:

* lung disease mechanisms

* COPD

* translational lung research

Why relevant:

BreathScope provides digital respiratory data, which fits translational research.

---

## **Jürgen Behr**

Professor of Pneumology

Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich

Director of Department of Medicine V.

Research fields:

* COPD

* pulmonary fibrosis

* pulmonary hypertension

Why relevant:

BreathScope could support clinical respiratory monitoring in rehabilitation.

---

## **Herbert Schiller**

Professor of Systems Biology of the Airways

Helmholtz Munich / LMU Munich

Research focus:

* systems biology

* lung disease analytics

* digital respiratory data

Why relevant:

BreathScope produces respiratory signal datasets, ideal for computational analysis.

---

# **Strategic Advantage**

Your profile combines three rare elements:

### **1 Clinical Physiotherapy Experience**

Direct patient rehabilitation work.

### **2 Digital Health Development**

Creation of BreathScope.

### **3 Real Clinical Deployment**

Use of the system in a rehabilitation clinic.

This combination is highly attractive for translational medical research.

---

## **PhD Research Proposal**

Digital Respiratory Monitoring in Pulmonary Rehabilitation

### **Candidate**

Moustafa Ali

Physiotherapist working in rehabilitation in Bavaria.

Developer of BreathScope, a browser-based respiratory volumetry tool currently used clinically at

Rosenhof Fachklinik.

---

## **Research Problem**

Respiratory physiotherapy lacks continuous objective monitoring tools.

Most clinical respiratory tests such as

* Spirometry

* Plethysmography

are not practical for frequent use during therapy sessions.

As a result, physiotherapists rely mainly on subjective assessment of breathing patterns and exercise tolerance.

---

## **Proposed Solution**

BreathScope is a browser-based respiratory analysis platform that enables:

• respiratory rate monitoring

• breathing amplitude estimation

• breathing pattern analysis

• therapy response tracking

The platform requires no software installation and minimal equipment, allowing easy integration into rehabilitation workflows.

---

## **Proposed Study**

Participants:

60 patients in pulmonary rehabilitation.

Target diseases:

* Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease

* Heart Failure

Measurements:

1 BreathScope respiratory signal analysis

2 Spirometry comparison

3 Functional capacity tests (6-Minute Walk Test)

---

## **Research Goal**

Evaluate whether digital respiratory monitoring can provide objective physiotherapy outcome measures during rehabilitation.

---

## **Potential Impact**

If validated, BreathScope could become a low-cost digital respiratory assessment tool for:

• pulmonary rehabilitation clinics

• physiotherapy practices

• tele-rehabilitation programs

• chronic respiratory disease monitoring

---

## **Research Environment**

The project aligns strongly with the Munich lung research ecosystem, including:

* Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich

* Helmholtz Munich

* the Comprehensive Pneumology Center Munich.

These institutions provide an ideal environment for translational respiratory research combining clinical practice and digital health innovation.

# **PhD Strategy & Research Proposal – BreathScope**

---

## **Candidate Profile**

Moustafa Ali – Physiotherapist working in rehabilitation with a focus on respiratory therapy and digital health innovation.

Developer of BreathScope, a browser-based respiratory volumetry tool currently used clinically at

Rosenhof Fachklinik.

Strengths:

* Clinical physiotherapy experience

* Pulmonary rehabilitation expertise

* Digital health development

* Working prototype already deployed

---

## **Proposed PhD Topic**

Digital Volumetric Respiratory Monitoring in Pulmonary Rehabilitation: Development, Validation, and Clinical Integration

Goal: Evaluate whether digital respiratory volumetry can serve as a continuous assessment tool for physiotherapy and rehabilitation outcomes.

---

## **Research Problem**

Respiratory physiotherapy lacks simple, objective monitoring tools.

Limitations of current approaches:

* Subjective observation of breathing patterns

* Occasional pulmonary function tests (spirometry, plethysmography)

* Infrequent, snapshot measurements

Result: Therapy outcomes are poorly quantified, limiting personalized rehabilitation plans.

---

## **Innovation – BreathScope**

BreathScope: browser-based, digital respiratory analysis platform for physiotherapy and pulmonary rehabilitation.

Features:

* Respiratory rate monitoring

* Breathing amplitude estimation

* Breathing pattern analysis

* Therapy response tracking

Advantages:

* No software installation

* Privacy-friendly (local processing possible)

* Easily integrated into clinical workflows

* Already in use at Rosenhof Fachklinik

---

## **Initial Study Design**

Participants: 60 rehabilitation patients

Target Conditions:

* Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease

* Heart Failure

Measurements:

1. BreathScope respiratory signal analysis

2. Spirometry comparison

3. Functional capacity tests (6-Minute Walk Test)

Research Questions:

1. Can BreathScope estimate breathing amplitude trends related to tidal volume?

2. Can the system detect improvements in respiratory efficiency during physiotherapy?

3. Can respiratory pattern changes predict clinical improvement or deterioration?

---
